protocol.description:
This protocol lets a client ask the compositor to render liquid glass behind parts of its surfaces: the background is refracted along a curved rim, or frosted, and finished by crisp lines along its edge. The look of each style is compositor policy; clients only describe where the glass goes and which style it is.
The presence of the makshell_glass_manager_v1 global tells clients that glass is available.
Since version 2, clients can also learn how bright the background behind their glass is, to pick a text color that stays legible over it.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Existing glass objects are not affected.

entry.name: glass_exists
entry.summary: the surface already has a glass object

request.name: get_glass

description.summary: get the glass object for a surface

request.description: Creates a glass object for the given surface. If the surface already has one, the glass_exists protocol error is raised.

interface.name: makshell_glass_v1
interface.description:
Holds a list of glass shapes rendered behind the surface. The list is double-buffered state, applied on the next wl_surface.commit, and starts out empty.
Requests only change the pending list, which persists across commits. To replace the shapes, send clear, then add each shape, then commit.
If the surface is destroyed, this object becomes inert.

request.name: destroy
request.description: The glass is removed right away, without waiting for a commit.

entry.name: invalid_shape
entry.summary: a shape has a non-positive width or height

entry.name: clear
entry.summary: refraction only; the background stays sharp

entry.name: frosted
entry.summary: a flat blurred background with crisp edge lines; for menus, popovers and alerts

entry.name: transparent
entry.summary: nothing is drawn; the shape only marks where track_brightness measures

entry.name: liquid
entry.summary: a light blur through a lens, darkened a little; for controls floating over content

entry.name: bubble
entry.summary: a dark tint over a lens, for small labels

entry.name: control
entry.summary: a grey veil over a strong lens, inside a rim that catches the light, for control modules; it does not blur

entry.name: card
entry.summary: a tint like frosted glass's over a lens like liquid glass's, for notifications

entry.name: chip
entry.summary: a very wide blur under a light grey tint, inside an even rim; for small buttons

entry.name: window
entry.summary: frosted glass, for an active dialog

entry.name: window_inactive
entry.summary: a lighter tint than window's, for a dialog that isn't active

request.name: add_backdrop

description.summary: add a blur that fades out instead of ending at an edge

request.description: Appends a blurred area to the pending list, in surface-local logical coordinates. Rather than having an edge, it fades in from each side over the given distance, in logical pixels.

request.name: add_rounded_rect_with_tail

description.summary: add a rounded rectangle with a tail pointing down

request.description: Like add_rounded_rect, but the shape is a rounded rectangle above a small tail that points down, like a speech bubble's. Together they fill the given rectangle: the tail takes tail_height off its bottom.

arg.name: tail_center
arg.summary: where the tail's tip is, from the left

entry.name: pop
entry.summary: there at once, and fades out quickly

entry.name: slide
entry.summary: slides in from the right, and back out there

entry.name: grow
entry.summary: grows out of the point as it fades in, and goes at once

entry.name: quick
entry.summary: fades in almost at once, and out like fade

request.name: set_appear

description.summary: say how the surface comes and goes

request.description: Asks for an animation for when the surface appears, and for its disappearing. The point is in surface-local logical coordinates.

request.name: add_box

description.summary: add a rounded rectangle that can move around inside a rectangle

request.description: A rounded rectangle anywhere inside the given rectangle, in which the background is kept. To animate it, keep that rectangle the same, so that nothing has to be set up again every frame.

arg.name: box_x
arg.summary: the middle of the box, from the rectangle's left

arg.name: box_y
arg.summary: the middle of the box, from the rectangle's top

request.name: add_droplet

description.summary: melt a circle into the shape added last

request.description: A circle that merges smoothly with the shape added last and pulls away from it like a drop of liquid, in the coordinates of its rectangle. There can be up to four.

arg.name: blend
arg.summary: how far apart they still reach for each other

request.name: set_last_opacity
request.description: How opaque the shape added last is, from 0 to 1.

request.name: add_rotated_rect

description.summary: add a rounded rectangle at an angle

request.description: A rounded rectangle of box_width by box_height, turned clockwise about its center, which is the center of the given rectangle. That rectangle has to be big enough to hold all of it.

request.name: add_rounded_rect_with_top_tail

description.summary: add a rounded rectangle with a tail pointing up

request.description: Like add_rounded_rect_with_tail, but with the tail on top, pointing up.

arg.name: tail_center
arg.summary: where the tail's tip is, from the left

request.name: add_rounded_rect

description.summary: add a rounded rectangle of glass

request.description:
Appends a rounded rectangle to the pending list, in surface-local logical coordinates. The radius is clamped to half the smaller side. Shapes should not overlap; overlapping glass is rendered twice.
A non-positive width or height raises the invalid_shape protocol error.

request.name: track_brightness

description.summary: report the brightness behind the glass

request.description:
Asks the compositor to send brightness events for the background behind the first shape in the list, as it is before the glass is drawn over it. Tracking lasts until this object is destroyed.
Measuring has a cost, so only ask for it when the answer changes how the surface is drawn.

request.name: add_content_blur

description.summary: blur part of what the surface shows

request.description: Blurs the surface's own contents inside a rectangle, in surface-local logical coordinates, by a radius in logical pixels: for something that comes into view out of focus. The glass behind stays as it is. The rectangles are pending state like the shapes, and cleared with them.

event.name: brightness

description.summary: brightness of the background behind the glass

event.description: The average relative luminance of the background behind the first shape, from 0 (black) to 1000 (white). Sent once a measurement is available after track_brightness, then whenever it changes noticeably. How often the compositor measures, and what counts as noticeable, is compositor policy.
